patches.title: Awaited Session commit receipts for appended entries
patches.genericRuntimeRationale: Consumers of the Session archive need awaited, durable commit evidence (sessionId, entryId, content hash, optional entrySeq) to attribute messages exactly once and to reconcile crash windows; observer-only events cannot prove durability. Receipts are carried on the new message_finalized lifecycle event; the Session append API itself keeps its existing return contract. iris_agent#40 consolidates every supported append path (agent loop, direct appendMessage, pending-writes flush) onto one shared appendAndCommitMessage primitive so no valid durable append can bypass commit evidence.

patches.notes: entrySeq is optional because the in-memory Session abstraction does not expose the storage-layer sequence; storage backends may fill it in later. 0.83.1: message_finalized now also carries the committed message (commit evidence completeness). Feature 2 (iris_agent#40): the receipt is now crash-consistent via the durable commit journal (appendEntryWithReceipt atomic append+receipt, recoverPendingCommitReceipts replay, ackCommitReceipt) with no Iris semantics; latestForkCommit 18d059bf is the accepted runtime head. iris_agent#51: the JSONL journal was upgraded from a bare two-line appendFile (not a transactional boundary) to a self-describing framed journal (v1 frame = entry + receipt + monotonic seq + sha256 checksum in ONE line, fsync via the new optional FileSystem.syncFile capability before the append reports success). Torn tails quarantine with a typed diagnostic; mid-file corruption fails closed; marker-looking message text stays lossless. The backend publishes an explicit supportsCrashRecoverableReceipts capability (true only with fsync); Session falls back to publish-only receipts when the capability is absent. See PI-019. iris_agent#50: replay order is now authoritative (receipt_seq = entry_seq, same transaction; committed_at is diagnostics only) and recovery validates session id / entry type+role / recomputed canonical content hash before emitting or ACKing, quarantining integrity-failed rows with typed reasons. See PI-020.

patches.title: Hermetic, content-addressed model catalog generation
patches.genericRuntimeRationale: Any runtime consumer that needs reproducible builds and typed model catalogs (e.g. identity-level Context engines that pin the accepted runtime) must not have normal build/check/test depend on mutable third-party model catalogs (models.dev, NVIDIA NIM, OpenRouter, Vercel AI Gateway). The fork commits the content-addressed model snapshot (per-file sha256 + structureHash + source provenance) and regenerates TypeScript shards/aggregator offline from it; live refresh is an explicit, separately reviewed command. Tests no longer reference transient catalog member IDs.

patches.title: Crash-consistent SessionCommitReceipt journal (durable receipt outbox)
patches.genericRuntimeRationale: Any runtime consumer that attributes committed messages exactly once needs the durable append and the receipt to survive a crash between the append and the lifecycle publication. A generic commit journal (optional SessionStorage appendEntryWithReceipt recording the entry and its pending receipt atomically, readPendingCommitReceipts, ackCommitReceipt) lets a restarting harness replay missed message_finalized events without re-appending (no duplicate semantic commit) and with stable receipt identity (sessionId + entryId + contentHash). No Iris Context/Historian/Memory semantics enter Pi.
affectedSurfaces: SessionStorage optional journal methods (appendEntryWithReceipt / readPendingCommitReceipts / ackCommitReceipt)

patches.title: Framed, crash-safe JSONL entry+receipt journal with explicit durability capability
patches.genericRuntimeRationale: A generic runtime that persists Session entries to JSONL needs a crash-recoverable commit journal with a real durability boundary: one appendFile call is not a transactional boundary, so the entry and receipt must be one verifiable frame (version + monotonic seq + sha256 checksum) written and fsynced before the append reports success. The backend publishes an explicit capability (supportsCrashRecoverableReceipts) that is true only when the filesystem provides fsync; callers requiring crash recovery (iris_agent production) fail closed otherwise. Torn tails (the only corruption an interrupted single-process append can produce) quarantine with a typed diagnostic and never fabricate an ACK; mid-file corruption fails closed; legacy pre-framing marker files remain readable.
tests: packages/agent/test/harness/jsonl-journal-crash.test.ts (capability declaration, fsync-less fail-closed journal seam, publish-only fallback, fault injection at every truncation point, checksum bit-rot, marker-lossless, concurrent seq monotonicity, idempotent ack, legacy framing compat)

packages/agent/test/harness/sqlite-node.test.ts (existing SQLite journal suite still green)
patches.removalCondition: earendil-works/pi provides an equivalent framed/transactional JSONL journal with a documented fsync boundary and iris_agent consumes the released package.
patches.compatibilityRisk: low: additive; the new frame format only affects newly written journal lines, legacy files remain readable, and capability-less filesystems degrade to the pre-journal publish-only path.
patches.notes: Part of iris_agent#51 (torn-write/crash-safety of the JSONL entry+receipt journal). Framed v1 journal: ONE line per commit (entry + pending receipt + monotonic seq + sha256 checksum), fsync via the optional FileSystem.syncFile before the append reports success; supportsCrashRecoverableReceipts is true only with BOTH syncFile AND truncateFile. Review-hardened across three independent review rounds: (1) missing-newline append guard; (2) load-time physical torn-tail repair via FileSystem.truncateFile at UTF-8 BYTE-accurate offsets (TextEncoder, CJK-safe — a UTF-16 misaligned truncate would destroy the preceding committed frame); (3) torn ack-marker tails and torn bare-entry tails (valid JSON, structurally incomplete) quarantine with typed diagnostics instead of throwing invalid_entry and bricking the session. Torn tails quarantine with a typed diagnostic (sticky, bounded per backend instance); mid-file corruption fails closed; legacy pre-framing marker files remain readable; marker-looking message text stays lossless. Status moves to carried after the accepted-runtime advancement audit passes.

patches.title: Authoritative receipt replay order and quarantine of integrity-failed receipts
patches.genericRuntimeRationale: A generic runtime that replays commit receipts after a crash must replay in the durable append order (not timestamp order) and must never emit or acknowledge a receipt whose identity does not match its durable entry (session id, entry type/role, recomputed canonical content hash). Integrity failures are quarantined with a typed reason and remain visible for health diagnostics without blocking later receipts or other sessions.
